explanations: In accepted(), the byte total is updated with a plain this.view[SLOT_BYTES] += BigInt(bytes), a non-atomic read-modify-write on shared memory. Several workers run accepted() in parallel, so increments interleave and are lost; it also races with drainCounters' Atomics.exchange on the main thread. telemetry.bytes is therefore under-reported under load. It should use Atomics.add(this.view, SLOT_BYTES, BigInt(bytes)).

Atomics.exchange returns the old value and writes 0 indivisibly, so any worker increment lands either before (and is reported) or after (and is kept for the next flush). Atomics.load works fine on BigInt64Array, waking is Atomics.notify, and resetting to 0 makes the reported values deltas, not monotonic.

begin() adds and end() subtracts, so the slot represents current in-flight frames. Zeroing it mid-flight would leave pending end() calls to push it below zero. Workers, not the main thread, write it; there is no slot limit on drainCounters; speed is not the reason.

begin() increments inflight, the !frame branch calls stats.rejected() and returns, and the finally block still runs stats.end(), restoring inflight. Bytes and accepted are only updated in accepted(); return does not skip finally.
